subject: Biotechnology
title: Life Cycle Assessment
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Life Cycle Assessment.

hook.text: Is bioplastic really greener? Life cycle assessment measures environmental impact from raw material to disposal.

buildup.text: LCA tracks energy, water, emissions, and waste across a product's entire life — from cradle to grave.

discovery.text: Bio-based polyethylene from sugarcane has a negative carbon footprint — the plant absorbs more CO2 than production emits.

twist.text: Land-use change can flip results — clearing rainforest for sugarcane makes bio-PE worse than fossil plastic.

climax.text: Standardized LCA frameworks like ISO 14040 enable fair comparisons — ensuring green claims are backed by data.

punchline.text: Count every impact, compare fairly — LCA separates greenwashing from real sustainability.

quiz.question: How can land-use change affect the LCA of bio-based products?
options: It always improves the environmental score by adding more plant life
Clearing natural ecosystems for biomass crops can increase carbon emissions enough to cancel the product's benefits
Land-use change only affects water consumption, not carbon emissions

details.summary: Life cycle assessment measures the total environmental impact of a product from raw material extraction through manufacturing, use, and disposal. In biotechnology, it determines whether bio-based products truly offer environmental benefits compared to conventional alternatives.
details.whyItMatters: Without rigorous LCA, bio-based products may claim sustainability while actually having higher impacts when full supply chains are considered. LCA provides the evidence base for genuine environmental decision-making.
takeaways: LCA evaluates environmental impact from cradle to grave of a product
It prevents greenwashing by quantifying real impacts across full supply chains
Bio-based products do not always outperform conventional alternatives in LCA

faq.question: What environmental categories does a life cycle assessment evaluate?
faq.answer: LCA measures greenhouse gas emissions, water use, land use, energy consumption, acidification, eutrophication, and toxicity across a product's entire lifecycle. Each category may tell a different story about overall environmental performance.

faq.question: Can bio-based products sometimes have worse environmental impacts?
faq.answer: Yes. Biofuels requiring intensive agriculture may cause more land-use change and water pollution than fossil fuels. Bio-plastics may need more energy to produce. LCA reveals these tradeoffs, ensuring decisions are based on data rather than assumptions.
